drafts.text:
levels just made hotels bookable from inside an AI agent.

so guests' agents will start asking hotels questions at 2am.

a 20-room amsterdam boutique hotel has nobody awake to answer. rates live in one tool, house rules in a pdf.

a company brain is how the hotel answers: rooms, rates, policies, past guests in one place. then skills that reply and book direct.
drafts.rides: levelsio 'Hotelist… works as an MCP connector so you can find, book and review hotels via your favorite AI agent' (25.4K views) + 'Hotelist is now my most popular site with 700,000+ visitors per month' (73.1K) + rauchg 'the future of software engineering is agents talking to other agents, even across different companies' (39.6K)

you can't hire the night desk, the review replier or the revenue analyst.

so: one company brain with your own rooms, rates and guest history. skills for the hours nobody covers. a human approves anything a guest sees.

that's the headcount you were missing.
drafts.rides: tibo_maker 'Hiring 101 (2026 edition): hire smart people, pay them well, give them unlimited AI tokens…' (14.9K views) + levelsio 'X should have a zero tolerance policy for AI replies' (249K)

drafts.text:
"saas is dead" is the headline.

for an amsterdam boutique hotel the real question is smaller: how many nights did we already sell that could have come direct?

i build a free sample from a hotel's own reviews and bookings that answers that.

if it can't show margin they'd win back, they shouldn't buy anything.
drafts.rides: gregisenberg 'SaaS is dead… where it's going in 11 minutes' video (101.4K views, 1,749 bookmarks) + gregisenberg 'a ton of fake ARR numbers out there' (25.4K) + mattshumer_ 'Every company says they're AI-native. I've seen exactly one.' (now 124.4K, 1,289 bookmarks)

video_tip: Video tip: 30–40s vertical screen recording, 'the guest's agent asks, the hotel answers': open on an AI agent asked for 'a quiet boutique hotel in the Jordaan for 2 nights', then cut to an anonymised Amsterdam boutique hotel's company brain answering that agent's questions (rate, late check-in, house rules) and offering the direct-booking link, ending on the nights-of-margin math. It mirrors levelsio's Hotelist-as-MCP-connector post (25.4K) and the format of AlexFinn's pages-and-dashboards video (now 321.6K, 5,261 bookmarks).

summary.headline: Guests' AI agents are starting to book hotels; the hotel needs a brain that can answer them.
summary.takeaway: Ride levelsio's Hotelist MCP moment: a 20-room Amsterdam boutique hotel has nobody to answer an agent at 2am, so one company brain plus approved skills is the missing headcount, proven with a free sample that shows recoverable margin.
